annotations.title: Get the audience: people vs machines

description: Returns who reached this site in the reporting window, counted as two populations that are NEVER summed — the audience doctrine: a machine fetch is not a human visit, so no combined total exists anywhere in this payload and none should be computed from it. `people` is the human half — clicks the search engines themselves reported, visits AI assistants sent, and, when the owner has connected Google Analytics, the site’s whole analytics audience with the two named routes as shares of it. `machines` is crawler/agent requests to this site, split into ordinary pages and agent files, with the impostor count. `limits` states what these numbers cannot say, per half — quote them before generalising about "the audience".
name: agentimus-read-audience

limits.description: What these numbers cannot say — each entry present only when true for THIS site, so never boilerplate.

scope.description: Which half the limit is about: humans, machines, or both.

agents.description: Distinct agents, by the name each declared.

fetches.description: Crawler/agent requests in the window, refused ones left out. Holds ordinary pages too when `pagesCounted` is true.

files.description: Of `fetches`, the agent files (llms.txt, .md twins, discovery documents, sitemap). pages + files = fetches.

from.description: First day of the window these four numbers cover (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC).

impostors.description: Clients caught claiming an identity verification did not support.

pagesCounted.description: Whether `fetches` can hold page reads: page logging is on, or page reads are still in the window. FALSE ⇒ agent files only.

to.description: Last day of that window — today, in UTC.

hasPrev.description: False on a first window — never invent a percentage from a zero baseline.

pages.description: Where those readers landed — the pages earning the citations.

prev.description: The window before this one, same length, no overlap.

sources.description: Distinct assistants seen — the full count, not the capped leaderboard.

visits.description: People an AI assistant sent, counted when the visit still carries a recognisable referrer or campaign tag — an assistant that strips both is invisible, so treat this as a minimum.

aiSessions.description: GA4’s own count of sessions AI assistants sent. Null = GA4 has no opinion yet, which is a different answer from zero.

connected.description: Whether Google Analytics is connected AND has usable numbers.

engineSessions.description: GA4’s per-engine organic arrivals, summed. Null on snapshots that predate the split.

error.description: The last fetch failure, when pending.

fetched.description: Unix time of the snapshot; 0 = never.

pending.description: Connected in Settings but never successfully polled — a fetch is what is missing, not the connection.

stale.description: True when the snapshot is over two days old.

start.description: First day the snapshot covers (Y-m-d), as Google was asked for it. When `stale` is true these are NOT the last `window` days — quote these dates instead.

users.description: Active users — the headline metric is PEOPLE, not sessions or views.

arrived.description: The human headline: analytics users when connected, otherwise search clicks + readers from AI. A sum of PEOPLE only — machines are never in it.

clicks.description: People, by the engines’ own reports — but the engines fold AI Overview appearances into these figures with no separating dimension.

pageCap.description: Always 0 now: no source samples a fixed set of pages. Kept so older readers of this payload keep taking their no-sampling path.

source.description: Which engines these clicks came from ("Google", "Bing", "Google + Bing") — quote it, never assume.

start.description: Widest window any connected source reports (YYYY-MM-DD); the engines publish on a delay, so it ends before today.

waiting.description: Pages Bing has not been asked about yet — it answers one page per request, so page-level detail fills in over days. The site-wide clicks here are whole either way. 0 for Google, which reports every page at once.

whole.description: True when `arrived` is the whole audience (analytics connected); false = the two named routes only, a smaller claim.

title: Get the audience: people vs machines
